title: SSO/SAML & RBAC packaging experiment: mandatory vs add-on bundling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Run a controlled experiment to determine whether requiring SSO/SAML and enterprise RBAC as contractual obligations (i.e., included by default for certain tiers) materially changes enterprise procurement velocity, average contract value, and post-sale support burden compared to offering them as priced add-ons.

Background: Sales and Legal have reported inconsistent asks from prospects: some require SSO + strict RBAC as a gating security control; others view those features as optional premium controls. Packaging strategy (mandatory vs add-on) affects pricing, SLAs, implementation timelines, and security questionnaire responses. We need data to recommend a default contract position and guardrails for negotiated exceptions.

Experiment hypothesis: Bundling SSO + RBAC into a named Enterprise tier (no additional line-item charge) will reduce sales cycle time by 15% for mid-market to enterprise deals and increase win-rate for security-sensitive prospects, but may lower average price-per-seat unless we raise base-tier price accordingly. Conversely, keeping SSO/RBAC as add-ons preserves price flexibility and upsell motion but may increase legal negotiation time and complexity of contract templates.

Success metrics (primary):
- Decrease in average sales cycle (opportunity created -> contract signed) for deals requiring SSO/SAML by >=15%
- Change in average TCV for deals with SSO/RBAC requirements (target: +5% or no worse than -3%)
- Reduction in contract negotiation touchpoints (legal reviews/revisions) by >=20%
- Security questionnaire turnaround time (customer-security-team response) improvement of >=25%

Secondary metrics:
- Number of closed-won deals where SSO/RBAC negotiation was the primary blocker
- Post-sale support tickets attributable to SSO onboarding (per 100 seats)

Plan & phases:
1) Draft contract language (Legal) for two conditions: a) Enterprise tier includes SSO + RBAC as standard, b) SSO/RBAC as billable add-ons with clear implementation SLAs. Produce a comparison table of terms and escalation paths. (Owner: Legal, due 2025-02-20)
2) Create variant pricing pages and one-pager for Sales (PM + Growth) for A/B split. Implement toggles in quoting tool to select "Bundled Enterprise" vs "Base + Add-ons." (Owner: Growth & Sales Ops, due 2025-02-28)
3) Run a 6-week pilot with Sales across matched cohorts (region and ARR segment) with randomized assignment to pricing/contract variant. Track wins, time to close, and negotiation notes. (Owner: Sales + PM)
4) Engage Solutions Engineering to prepare an onboarding checklist and estimate implementation lead times for each variant. Include average SOW hours. (Owner: Solutions Eng)
5) Post-pilot review with Legal, Sales, Finance, Security to finalize recommendation and adjust playbooks. (Owner: PM)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- If we bundle SSO/RBAC the base price may need a lift; what price elasticity is acceptable? (Finance + Growth input required)
- How do marketplace and partner channel contracts interact with mandatory packaging?
- Operational burden: will bundling increase early-stage onboarding tickets and SLA exposure? Solutions Eng and Support need to model headcount impact.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Bundling leads to lower ASP. Mitigation: model tier price changes and target increases; test small cohorts first.
- Risk: Security/Legal pushback on fixed-term commitments for RBAC guarantees. Mitigation: offer a clear exception process and negotiate retention/rollback clauses.

- Begin randomized pilot on 2025-03-03 for 6 weeks.
- Collect feedback loop with Security to capture questionnaire time savings and standard answers for each variant.
